question: Which one of the following is the largest natural freshwater lake in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wular**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wular Lake**, located in **Jammu and Kashmir**, is the largest natural freshwater lake in India.
 
• It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia and is fed by the **Jhelum River**.
 
• The **lake plays a crucial role in the local ecosystem**, supporting a variety of wildlife and acting as a flood reservoir by absorbing excess water during heavy rains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Barapani**:

 
 
• Also known as **Umiam Lake**, Barapani is an artificial reservoir in **Meghalaya**.
 
• It was created by damming the Umiam River for hydroelectric power generation, so it is not a natural freshwater lake.
 
 
 
• **Bhimtal**:
 
 
• **Bhimtal is a lake in the town of Bhimtal, near Nainital city in Nainital district of Kumaon**, India with a masonry dam built in 1883 creating the storage facility.
 
• It is th**e largest lake of Nainital district, as well as Kumaon**, which is known as the "Lake district of India".
 
• It's th**e 2nd largest lake by surface area in Uttarakhand. **
 
• **The lake provides drinking water supply and supports aquaculture with variety of fish species. **
 
 
 
• **Loktak**:
 
 
• Loktak Lake, located in **Manipur**, is the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India.
 
• It is famous for its **phumdis** (floating islands), but it is not as large as Wular Lake.
